proposal.summary: You force yourself back onto your feet and keep running down the open road, not stopping to look back.

outcomes.text: You're up and running, the Nest Warden's pursuit settling into a grim rhythm at your back — no ground gained, none lost.
You scramble up and put a real stretch of road behind you, lungs burning, the sound of it behind you thinning a little.
Something corrects your stride again before a stumble can take you down, and you run on steadier than your legs have any right to manage.
Somewhere behind you a snarl breaks off into a heavy weight hitting the ground that isn't yours, and whatever was closing on you doesn't close any further.
For the length of the run you feel a solid weight pacing exactly at your left heel, one you could lean into on the turns, and there is nothing there when you risk the glance.
The line of paw-prints keeping pace beside yours on the road turns, mid-stride, to face back the way you came — and stays turned that way even as you keep moving forward.
